entrypoints.summary: The observed failure path enters bt_accept_dequeue during l2cap_sock_cleanup_listen and L2CAP socket release.
Fixed L2CAP source shows listener-state cleanup calling l2cap_sock_cleanup_listen; the report identifies that cleanup path as the bt_accept_dequeue caller.

sources.concept: L2CAP listener cleanup dequeues an accepted Bluetooth socket

impact.affected_asset: Lifetime and memory safety of an accepted Bluetooth socket object (struct sock).
impact.attacker_capability: Cause execution to reach the demonstrated cleanup/dequeue lifetime error in the fuzzed kernel environment; broader attacker reachability or exploitation is not established.
impact.security_effect: Kernel slab use-after-free write detected by KASAN during Bluetooth L2CAP listener cleanup.

causal_trace.summary: Listening L2CAP socket cleanup reaches bt_accept_dequeue while processing accepted sockets.

Before the fix, bt_accept_dequeue dropped the temporary reference obtained by bt_accept_get before bt_accept_unlink; unlink then dropped the queue reference, leaving no retained reference to keep the socket allocated before a caller reference was acquired.
A subsequent sock_hold refcount increment in bt_accept_dequeue accessed the socket after it had been freed through bt_accept_unlink.
KASAN reported a slab use-after-free write at the refcount increment, with the free trace traversing bt_accept_unlink and the cleanup call chain.

failure.operation: sock_hold()/refcount increment on a freed struct sock in bt_accept_dequeue

primary_invariant.kind: socket reference ownership across accept-queue unlink
primary_invariant.statement: A socket returned from accept-queue dequeue must retain a live reference across unlink and until ownership is transferred to the successful caller or explicitly released on a non-returning path.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The pre-fix path released the bt_accept_get temporary reference before unlink consumed the queue reference, then attempted to take a caller reference after the object could already have been freed.

raw_refs.role: KASAN issue record and crash trace
syzbot report mirrored to mailing list

quality.review_notes: Primary crash and upstream fix provide a concrete ownership mechanism and KASAN oracle. The syzbot mailing-list report states that no reproducer was available at report time; retained artifacts establish fuzz-observed failure but do not establish a network-remote trigger, a standalone deterministic reproducer, or exploitability beyond the observed invalid write.

remediation.invariant_restored: The fix retains the bt_accept_get queue-walk reference through bt_accept_unlink, hands that live reference to the caller on success, and explicitly drops it on closed or not-yet-connected paths.
mitigation_classes: explicit reference release on non-returning paths

oss_fuzz.crash_state: Observed KASAN report; report states no standalone reproducer was available at filing.
oss_fuzz.fuzz_target: Linux Bluetooth L2CAP listener cleanup and accept dequeue path

state_context.attacker_state_setup: A syzbot-generated execution reached listener cleanup with an accepted socket in the relevant accept-queue lifecycle. The supplied evidence does not retain the triggering program.
data_structure_invariants: The accept queue retains a reference while a child socket is queued.
The temporary reference returned by bt_accept_get must survive bt_accept_unlink when the socket is returned.
Each retained reference must be explicitly released when a dequeue iteration does not return the socket.
state_context.state_machine: The observed path is L2CAP listener cleanup, which dequeues queued accepted sockets; the patch separately handles closed and not-yet-connected cases.

target.component: Bluetooth AF_BLUETOOTH accept queue and L2CAP listener cleanup

oracle.expected_negative: With the fixed ownership transfer, the same cleanup/dequeue path should not produce that KASAN use-after-free report.
oracle.expected_positive: On the affected code path, KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free write in sock_hold/refcount increment within bt_accept_dequeue.
